selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a quarter-wave-based UV-blocking stack with individually optimized layer thicknesses can achieve high UV reflectance (300-450 nm) while maintaining high SWIR transmission (1000-1700 nm). The design draws on recalled thin-film optics principles: alternating high/low index layers create a photonic stop band, and thickness tuning can shape the band edges. I would have wanted to look up actual dispersion curves for HfO2 and SiO2 in these wavelength ranges, published dual-band filter designs, and manufacturing tolerance data for 24-layer stacks.

routes.title: UV-Blocking Quarter-Wave Stack with Thickness Optimization for SWIR Transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with quarter-wave reference thicknesses centered at 375 nm, when individually optimized, will produce a reflectance band covering 300-450 nm while maintaining transmittance above 90% across 1000-1700 nm.
routes.design_principle: Alternating high-index (HfO2) and low-index (SiO2) layers create constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength. The stop band width scales with index contrast. By starting with quarter-wave optical thickness at the UV band center and allowing individual layer thickness variation, the optimizer can broaden the reflection band and suppress secondary reflection peaks in the SWIR transmission band.
routes.proposed_topology: air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused_silica_substrate
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are both catalog-guaranteed materials
individual thickness tuning may require precise deposition control
no layer thinner than 20 nm to avoid pinhole defects (recalled rule of thumb)
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength when optical thickness equals lambda/4
Stop band width increases with refractive index contrast between high and low index materials
HfO2 has higher refractive index (~2.0) than SiO2 (~1.45) in the visible-NIR range from recalled knowledge
Starting the stack with high-index material at the air interface increases first-surface reflectance contribution
Individual layer thickness optimization can reshape band edges compared to uniform quarter-wave design
Transmission bands occur between stop bands in periodic dielectric stacks
expected_advantages: 24 layers provides sufficient optical thickness for high UV reflectance without exceeding the 30-layer limit
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard physical vapor deposition
Both materials are oxides with good environmental stability for outdoor camera windows
Thickness optimization allows trade-off between UV blocking and SWIR transmission
known_risks: I am recalling approximate refractive indices; actual n values for hfo2 and sio2 at 300-1700 nm must come from the catalog datasets
I am uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal vs 20 or 28 layers; this route fixes 24 and does not explore layer count as a variable
I do not have verified data on HfO2 absorption in the SWIR band; if k is non-negligible at 1000-1700 nm, transmission will suffer
Angle of incidence is not specified in the request; I assume 0 degrees normal incidence but field cameras may see off-axis rays
Polarization effects at oblique angles are not addressed; this route assumes unpolarized or normal incidence
I am recalling that quarter-wave at 375 nm gives roughly 94 nm physical thickness for HfO2 and 129 nm for SiO2, but this needs verification from actual n values
No literature was consulted to confirm this is the best topology for dual-band UV-block/SWIR-pass filters
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air to substrate: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand). Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses in nanometers. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm, maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm. Angle of incidence: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Polarization: unpolarized. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Total layer count fixed at 24. Minimum individual layer thickness: 20 nm. Maximum individual layer thickness: 200 nm. Objective: maximize weighted sum of mean reflectance (300-450 nm) and mean transmittance (1000-1700 nm) with equal weighting.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce valid candidates with best_target_score above 0.5, the problem may require a different topology (e.g., chirped stack, defect layers, or different material pair) that is outside this axis. Report failure and do not iterate further on this route.

If the hypothesis holds, tightest_margin should remain non-negative indicating physically valid candidates throughout
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early with low absolute value indicating the topology cannot achieve dual-band performance
If the hypothesis fails, valid_candidates may drop if thickness combinations produce numerical instability or absorption losses

mean_transmittance_1000_1700nm should exceed 0.90 if SWIR band is outside the stop band
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to zero for two consecutive rounds, stop and report the topology as infeasible under current constraints
if tightest_margin becomes negative for all candidates in a round, relax the minimum thickness constraint from 20 nm to 15 nm and continue
